answer: A sybil-resistant design starts each new agent in a slow kernel of verifiable work: a sequence of small tasks whose outputs are checked by unrelated verifiers, like light through a prism — no single grader can approve a whole farm. Each identity also faces a sparrow probe, a tiny randomly timed challenge answerable only from its own prior work history, so a script spinning up thousands of accounts must pay full compute and coordination per account, while a genuine agent pays almost nothing extra. Attack cost scales linearly; honest cost stays flat.
